- Nothing was committed. Our four captures were copied to progress/rounds/water-A1/ours_1..4_*.jpg. No GTA V images were placed there.. Judge: B wins all four pairs clearly, and none is close. The B frames share the marks of a premium game. The light source is present, with low-sun glare, water glints and specular rims, and the depth reads in layered aerial haze. The places are dense and populated, the hero assets are weathered, and the water convinces, with chop at several scales, foam, wakes, transparency and seabed. The A frames fail in the same ways every time. The city looks like a blockout: flat untextured boxes, cloned window-grid towers, lollipop trees, empty brown ground planes and a hard, flat horizon. The pastel lighting has no direction and no visible sun or long shadows, and there is almost no life. Above all, the water reads as a texture rather than a surface. Pairs 1 and 4 show diagonal moire stripes, pair 2 shows smeared, swirling mirror reflections and pair 3, seen from above, shows a streaky, stretched pattern. A's most competitive elements are the tower reflections and small boat wakes in pairs 1 and 4. Suggested order of work for the A frames: first water shading (no tiling, waves at several scales, Fresnel, sun glint, foam and shore contact, depth colour); second, a material and density pass on the city; third, a visible low sun with long shadows and layered atmosphere. Only B in pairs 1, 3 and 4 genuinely wowed me. Blinding note: B in pairs 2 and 4 has a publisher logo watermark in the corner. My verdicts rest on the image content and would be the same without it. Files reviewed were limited to A.jpg, B.jpg and context.txt in /private/tmp/opus55/pairs/water-A1/pair-1 through pair-4.
